LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is for firefox-esr-i18n-pa-in, part of the standard Firefox ESR packaging on Arch Linux. The top-level code (which executes during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`) consists of standard variable assignments (pkgbase, pkgname, pkgver, pkgver, source arrays, sha512sums, etc.) and two for-loops.

The first for-loop iterates over a static `_languages` array and uses `eval` to define `package_*` functions. This eval only constructs function definitions from hardcoded static data — it does not execute arbitrary external code, download payloads, or exfiltrate data. The function bodies call `_package_i18n`, which is only invoked during `package()`, not during `--printsrcinfo`.

The second for-loop populates the `noextract` array via string manipulation and case matching — purely local, safe operations. The `_google_api_key` is a hardcoded constant (a well-known Arch-shared Google API key for Firefox builds, as noted in the comments), not a value exfiltrated from local files. No top-level command substitutions, network calls, or dangerous commands (curl/wget/eval-of-dynamic-content) are present in the global scope.

All packaging functions (prepare, build, package_firefox-esr) are function definitions and do not execute during this step, so they are out of scope for this gate.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Top-level code is standard packaging; no malicious execution during source.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
